clue.text: Plant — wrong term for scented root — added by one who served under 25

parts.note: a herb is a plant

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are set into a new arrangement

parts.note: orris root is the fragrant root of an iris, used in perfumery
on, as in 'and so on', means in addition

explanation.surface: A gardening note about an iris root, oddly signed off by a wartime underling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles the letters of term into ERTM. Herbert Morrison was Home Secretary in Churchill's wartime coalition, hence 'served under 25'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Morrison, Labour politician, held office as Home Secretary in Churchill's wartime cabinet.

clue.text: Greeting broadcast to back row at gunpoint — setter's chiefly got himself to blame

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting
seed broadcast is sown, scattered over the field

indicators.note: back means the word row is read backwards

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
the word's second half, point, gives E, east, a point of the compass
the setter speaking of himself says my

explanation.surface: Someone shouting a greeting to the back row while held at gunpoint brought the trouble on himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the seating row from right to left, and 'gunpoint' splits into gun and point; 'chiefly' and 'at' are padding. Bevin's quip in 22 answers this phrase about Morrison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is the main cause of his own troubles is said, idiomatically, to be harmful chiefly to himself.

clue.text: Journalist's piece about wine

parts.note: re means concerning or about
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A newspaper article covering wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a news story written by a journalist.

clue.text: Provide flexibility for cities confused after disposal arises

indicators.note: after places the scrambled cities letters behind the reversed piece
in a down clue arising means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a sale is a disposal of goods

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Muddled cities need loosening up once a sell-off happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arises' turns SALE into ELAS; 'confused' rearranges CITIES into TICISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elasticise something is to make it stretchy, giving it flexibility.

clue.text: Athenian name and French one? It's the other way round

indicators.note: the other way round asks for each piece to be read backwards in place

parts.note: nom is the French word for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a Greek name and its French equivalent, said to be reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' turns each piece in place, keeping their order. Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's misanthrope; 'It' looks like part of the instruction but is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens, title character of Shakespeare's play, was a citizen of Athens.

clue.text: Western town's story about a beast

indicators.note: about means the story goes around the beast

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
a ram is a male sheep, a beast

explanation.surface: A Wild West settlement's tale concerning an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' tempts as the Western's plot, but it is the falsehood that wraps round the animal; 'about' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Laramie in Wyoming is a town of the American West, famed in cowboy films and television.

clue.text: 2 of light to test 4 — it keeps cropping up

indicators.note: 2 down is REPORT, so a report of the word means it as heard

parts.note: the word light, said aloud
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Testing a reported light keeps coming round.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '4' is not 4 down but the number, in Roman numerals. LEITMOTIV is the German spelling of leitmotif.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotiv is a recurring musical or literary theme that returns throughout a work.

clue.text: Valley of the lute?

definitions.meaning: a ... valley is a long valley formed by a fault
Tennyson's 'little ... within the lute' is a small crack that spoils the music

explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a crack or split, whether a geological valley or a flaw in an instrument.

clue.text: See 1 across
Advice to games players on confrontational features?

definitions.meaning: players are told to keep an eye on the ball, read here as the answer
an eyeball-to-eyeball meeting is a direct confrontation

explanation.definitionFit: Eyeballs are the organs of sight, and to eyeball someone is to stare them down.

clue.text: Relation covered in water or ink

indicators.note: covered in means the ratio sits inside the water

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
pi is a mathematical relation, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter

explanation.surface: A family member is soaked in water or ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a relative, but it is the ratio pi.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the brown ink from the cuttlefish.

clue.text: Sheer compulsion is what supplies water to waterfall

parts.note: a water main brings water to homes
force is a northern English dialect word for a waterfall

explanation.surface: Something about the plumbing that feeds a cascade.
explanation.walkthrough: FORCE as a waterfall is a northern English usage, as in High Force in County Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: Main force means sheer physical strength or compulsion, as in 'by main force'.

clue.text: See 1 down
Addition to passport not altogether advisable

indicators.note: not altogether means only part of the word advisable is used

explanation.surface: A passport stamp that is not wholly wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an endorsement added to a passport allowing entry to a country.

clue.text: How we see health food — silver put into nickel (twice)

parts.note: bran is the fibrous husk eaten as a health food

indicators.note: put into means the silver goes inside the coin

parts.note: a nickel is five cents, so two of them make a dime
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A health food described as silver set into coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' places the silver inside the coin, giving DIMAGE; a dime is the US ten-cent coin, worth two nickels.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand image is how the public perceives a brand.

clue.text: Nobleman with sword protecting queen from stub

indicators.note: protecting means the nobleman and sword surround the queen

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
a foil is a fencing sword
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A swordsman aristocrat guards a queen from a stub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' means the noble and the blade stand either side of the monarch; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfoil is the stub of a cheque or ticket kept as a record.

clue.text: Being no scholar, three pieces of Ban Ki-Moon follow his body — don't tell anyone!

indicators.note: follow places the name's pieces after the body

parts.note: Ban Ki-Moon headed the UN, so his body is the United Nations
B, OO and KI are three bits lifted from the name Ban Ki-Moon
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: The UN chief, no intellectual, is told to keep quiet about his organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces are B (from Ban), KI and OO (from Moon), arranged as B-OO-KI; Ban Ki-Moon was UN Secretary General.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbookish means not given to reading or study, hence no scholar.

clue.text: Toadstool for hanging judge?

definitions.meaning: a judge passing a death sentence put on a black cap

explanation.definitionFit: The death cap is a toadstool, and the black cap was what British judges wore to sentence someone to death.

clue.text: Viv Richards is opposed to a breaking shooter

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: breaking means the letter a splits the gun

parts.note: a gun is a shooter

explanation.surface: A cricket legend is against someone breaking a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts A inside GUN for GUAN. Viv Richards is the great West Indies batsman from Antigua.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Viv Richards, the West Indies cricketer, was born on Antigua, so he is one of its people.

clue.text: Queen at home for some drinks — at home to one who served under 25

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a nest is a home
bev, short for beverage, means drink
in means at home

explanation.surface: A queen hosts drinks at home for a wartime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Bevin was Minister of Labour in Churchill's wartime coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Bevin, Labour politician, served as Minister of Labour under Churchill in the war.

clue.text: See 22
Bilingual acknowledgement of paternity in a measure

parts.note: I am, in English, the first half of a claim to be someone's parent
pere is French for father, finishing the claim in the other language

explanation.surface: A man admits fatherhood in two languages, to some degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am pere' switches from English to French halfway, hence 'Bilingual'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampere is the unit used to measure electric current.

clue.text: Prelapsarian journey?

parts.note: prelapsarian means before the fall, and a stumble is what comes before one, as well as a journey

explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey, and also a stumble that comes before a fall.

clue.text: "Home when all initiative falters" (18, when told "1 across 7 is 1 down 11")

indicators.note: faltering letters stumble out of place, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slogan says a household fails when its drive gives out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Bevin, told that Herbert Morrison was his own worst enemy, is said to have replied with this line.
explanation.definitionFit: This was Ernest Bevin's reported retort on hearing a colleague called his own worst enemy.

clue.text: Monsters out of hospital go to fatherland

indicators.note: out of means the hospital letter is removed

parts.note: whales are sea monsters

explanation.surface: Monsters discharged from hospital head for their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh anthem is 'Land of My Fathers', hence fatherland.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is the land of my fathers in its national anthem, so a fatherland.

clue.text: Trauma over borough?

parts.note: a lasting mark of trauma placed above the word borough makes a Yorkshire seaside town

explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting mark left by a wound or trauma.

clue.text: Ben following his follower in small volume by writer and painter

indicators.note: following puts the mountain after the rest
in means the follower sits inside the small volume

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a small volume
Ben is followed by Hur in Ben-Hur
a ben is a Scottish mountain, a hill

explanation.surface: A writer and artist is produced by a small book and its sequel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' does double service in the surface: as a hill, and as the start of Ben-Hur whose follower is HUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill won the Nobel Prize for Literature and was a keen amateur painter.

clue.text: See 22
Writer takes to painting — his first is in 23

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
painting is an art

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of his

explanation.surface: A writer takes up painting; his first work is in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Penarth is a seaside town near Cardiff in Wales.

clue.text: Queen's authority would see ghost if political correctness were exchanged

indicators.note: political correctness is PC, and exchanging those two letters turns one word into the other

parts.note: a spectre is a ghost

explanation.surface: The monarch's power would look spooky if correct politics changed places.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the P and C of SPECTRE and you get SCEPTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the staff a monarch holds as the emblem of sovereign authority.
